title: Choose the visual world for HR Assistant
question: The roll assigned the Annual Report Grid. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Annual Report Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style bank annual reports
options.thesis: HR's day set like a bank's annual report: a strict grid, key figures at large size, and one red ink reserved for what only HR can decide.
options.viewport: Petrol-blue navigation rail on the left. The home page opens with the helper's one-line greeting, then a row of key figures (needs your decision, analysing, urgent mail, unverified senders) set large like a report's highlights, then the work queue as a ruled table. The assistant panel stays on the right.
options.risk: Can read cold if the grid is set timidly; the helper character has to carry the warmth.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: large figures against small labels, no cards or tiles to make things important.
One ink reserved for the active leg: red appears only on items waiting for HR's decision, nowhere decorative.
States as printed marks: flag severity drawn as filled, half and outline squares, never colour alone.
Destructive actions (delete, clear inbox) stand apart with deliberate empty space.
The helper gets a name plate and one fixed line, like a staff badge, so it reads as a colleague, not a toy.
Every item carries a stable reference number (CV-014, MAIL-007) used in the UI and the assistant's answers.

options.label: Passport Security Print
options.lineage: passport and visa page security printing
options.thesis: Every CV and email is a document crossing a border: guilloche-ruled pages, microtext rules, and HR's decision applied as an entry stamp.
options.viewport: Same shell and work queue; each queue row is a document slip, checks show as stamped marks, and a passed item carries a visa-style stamp.
options.risk: The most obvious picture for a security story; guilloche can slide into decoration and stamps into bureaucracy.

options.label: Variable type specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: HR and a jury don't identify with type specimens, and a working screen loses clarity.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.case: Fuses poorly: a map metaphor confuses a queue of CVs and emails.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active leg.

options.label: Centre-rail reference setting
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as a book, not a working tool, and cuts against the jury demo.

options.label: Character goods catalog
options.case: Fuses poorly: too playful for bank HR, which you ruled out.
options.kept: The helper as a named character with fixed personal details.

options.label: Dark-first developer console
options.case: Fuses poorly: a tool costume; HR managers don't live in consoles.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated by empty space.

options.label: Factory records catalog
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels hide meaning a jury must read at a glance.
options.kept: Stable catalog numbers for every item.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean HR SaaS dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a row of stat cards, charts and a recent-activity list, like your reference image.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design, the template look you ruled out.
